Korean: 음악 소리를 조금 줄여 주실 수 있을까요?
English: Could you turn down the music a little?

Korean: 출퇴근 거리 때문에 그 일자리 제안을 거절해야 했어요.
English: I had to turn down the job offer because of the commute.

Korean: 그녀는 이미 약속이 있어서 초대를 거절했어요.
English: She turned down the invitation because she already had plans.
Turn down the heat once the soup starts boiling.

Korean: 모두 들을 수 있게 소리를 높여 주실 수 있나요?
English: Can you turn up the volume so everyone can hear?
My missing keys turned up in my jacket pocket.

Korean: 그는 아무에게도 알리지 않고 늦게 나타났어요.
English: He turned up late without letting anyone know.

Korean: 계속 찾아보면 쓸 만한 게 나올 수도 있어요.
English: Something useful might turn up if we keep looking.
Please turn off the lights when you leave.
I turn off notifications while I'm working.

Korean: 강한 냄새 때문에 정말 내키지 않았어요.
English: The strong smell really turned me off.

Korean: 설정에서 자동 업데이트를 끌 수 있어요.
English: You can turn off automatic updates in the settings.

Korean: 여섯 시에 역 밖으로 데리러 갈게요.
English: I'll pick you up outside the station at six.

Korean: 집에 오는 길에 우유 좀 사 올 수 있나요?
English: Could you pick up some milk on your way home?

Korean: 여행하면서 유용한 표현 몇 개를 익혔어요.
English: I picked up a few useful phrases during my trip.

Korean: 보통 명절 무렵에는 장사가 활기를 띠어요.
English: Business usually picks up around the holidays.
Can you drop me off near the entrance?
I'll drop off the package before I go to work.
Sales dropped off after the promotion ended.
I dropped off while watching a documentary.
We need to put off the meeting until next week.

Korean: 통증이 계속되면 진료받는 걸 미루지 마세요.
English: Don't put off seeing a doctor if the pain continues.

Korean: 가격이 너무 비싸서 재킷을 살 마음이 사라졌어요.
English: The high price put me off buying the jacket.
I've been putting off organizing my desk.
Let me look up the address before we leave.
I looked up the word in an English dictionary.

Korean: 이 번호로 예약 내역을 조회할 수 있어요.
English: You can look up your booking using this number.

Korean: 우리 팀 상황이 드디어 나아지고 있어요.
English: Things are finally looking up for our team.

Korean: 결제가 왜 실패했는지 알아봐 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you look into why the payment failed?

Korean: 여행 비용을 줄일 수 있는 방법을 알아보고 있어요.
English: We're looking into cheaper options for the trip.

Korean: 관리자가 제 불만 사항을 확인해 보겠다고 약속했어요.
English: The manager promised to look into my complaint.
I'll look into the details and get back to you.

Korean: 제가 표를 사는 동안 가방 좀 봐 주실래요?
English: Would you look after my bag while I buy a ticket?
She looks after her parents on weekends.

Korean: 집을 비우는 동안 화분을 돌봐 줄 사람이 필요해요.
English: We need someone to look after the plants while we're away.

Korean: 일이 바빠질 때일수록 몸을 잘 챙겨야 해요.
English: You should look after yourself when work gets busy.
I'm looking forward to seeing you again.

Korean: 새 식당에 가 보는 걸 기대하고 있어요.
English: We're looking forward to trying the new restaurant.

Korean: 그녀는 새 직장에서 일하게 될 날을 기대하고 있어요.
English: She's looking forward to starting her new job.

Korean: 몇 주 전부터 이번 휴식을 기다려 왔어요.
English: I've been looking forward to this break for weeks.
We ran out of coffee this morning.

Korean: 휴대전화 저장 공간이 거의 다 찼어요.
English: I'm running out of space on my phone.
Make sure we don't run out of time.
The printer ran out of paper in the middle of the job.
I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.
We ran into a problem while installing the app.
Let me know if you run into any difficulties.

Korean: 여기서 당신을 만나게 될 줄은 몰랐어요.
English: I wasn't expecting to run into you here.
I can't figure out how to change the reservation.
We finally figured out what was causing the noise.
Give me a minute to figure this out.

Korean: 어떤 선택이 가장 잘 맞는지 알아봤어요?
English: Have you figured out which option suits you best?
I'll sort out the paperwork this afternoon.

Korean: 더 커지기 전에 이 오해를 풀어야 해요.
English: We need to sort out this misunderstanding before it gets worse.
Don't worry; we'll sort it out together.
I haven't sorted out my travel plans yet.
I work out at the gym twice a week.

Korean: 각자 얼마씩 내야 하는지 계산해 봐요.
English: Let's work out how much each person should pay.
I hope everything works out for you.

Korean: 두 팀 모두에게 맞는 일정을 마련했어요.
English: We worked out a schedule that suits both teams.

Korean: 예약 시간 전에 이 양식을 작성해 주세요.
English: Please fill out this form before your appointment.
I filled out the application online.
Do I need to fill out every section?
She helped me fill out the customs declaration.

Korean: 점심시간에 제 일을 잠깐 대신해 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you fill in for me during the lunch break?
I'll fill you in on what happened at the meeting.
Please fill in the missing information.

Korean: 관리자가 없는 동안 누군가 업무를 대신해야 해요.
English: Someone needs to fill in while the manager is away.

Korean: 탑승 수속이 마감되기 전에 체크인해야 해요.
English: I need to check in before the flight closes.
We checked in at the hotel around three.
I'll check in with you tomorrow to see how you're doing.
Can we check in a little earlier?
What time do we need to check out?
You should check out the new exhibition.
I'll check out the reviews before ordering.
We checked out of the hotel after breakfast.

Korean: 컴퓨터를 업데이트하기 전에 파일을 백업해 주세요.
English: Please back up your files before updating the computer.
I backed up my photos to an external drive.

Korean: 우리 결정에 대해 물어보면 제 말을 뒷받침해 주실 수 있나요?
English: Can you back me up if they ask about our decision?
Traffic is backed up for several kilometers.

Korean: 내일 화상 통화를 잡아 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you set up a video call for tomorrow?
I need help setting up my new phone.
They set up a small business last year.
We've set up a shared folder for the project.
I need to catch up on the work I missed.

Korean: 커피를 마시면서 그동안 어떻게 지냈는지 이야기해요.
English: Let's meet for coffee and catch up.
I walked faster to catch up with my friends.
I'll catch up on the news after dinner.
It's hard to keep up with all these changes.

Korean: 계속 잘해 주세요. 실력이 늘고 있어요.
English: Keep up the good work; you're making progress.

Korean: 함께 달리면 그를 따라갈 수가 없어요.
English: I can't keep up with him when we go running.
She keeps up with her friends through messages.
I'll get back to you after I check the schedule.
When did you get back from your trip?

Korean: 점심 전에 보고서 작업으로 돌아가야 해요.
English: I need to get back to the report before lunch.
Let's get back to the main topic.
How do you get along with your new coworkers?
We get along well despite our different opinions.

Korean: 여유 시간이 줄어든 생활에 적응하고 있어요.
English: I'm learning to get along with less free time.

Korean: 아이들은 함께 놀 때 보통 사이좋게 지내요.
English: The children usually get along when they play together.
It took me a week to get over the flu.

Korean: 아직 실망감을 떨쳐 내려고 노력하고 있어요.
English: I'm still trying to get over the disappointment.
We need to get over our fear of making mistakes.

Korean: 그녀는 마침내 비행기를 타는 두려움을 극복했어요.
English: She finally got over her fear of flying.
I couldn't get through to customer service.
Let's get through the urgent tasks first.

Korean: 당신의 도움이 힘든 시기를 버티는 데 도움이 됐어요.
English: Your support helped me get through a difficult time.
Have you managed to get through all the emails?
I'd like to bring up one more point.

Korean: 저녁 식사 중에는 그 문제를 꺼내지 말아 주세요.
English: Please don't bring up that issue during dinner.
She was brought up by her grandparents.

Korean: 그는 회의에서 프로젝트 비용 문제를 제기했어요.
English: He brought up the cost of the project at the meeting.

Korean: 더 나은 계획을 생각해 내야 해요.
English: We need to come up with a better plan.

Korean: 그녀는 시간을 절약할 간단한 방법을 생각해 냈어요.
English: She came up with a simple way to save time.

Korean: 예시를 몇 개 생각해 낼 수 있나요?
English: Can you come up with a few examples?
I'll try to come up with a name for the new service.
I don't want to give up just because it's difficult.
He gave up smoking last year.
Don't give up on your plans too soon.

Korean: 더 필요한 분에게 자리를 양보해야 했어요.
English: I had to give up my seat to someone who needed it more.

Korean: 제가 전화를 받는 동안 계속 진행해 주세요.
English: Please carry on while I answer this call.
We carried on working despite the noise.

Korean: 그녀는 취직한 뒤에도 공부를 계속할 계획이에요.
English: She plans to carry on studying after she gets a job.
You can carry on with the next exercise.
I ended up taking a taxi because I missed the last train.
We ended up staying longer than we expected.
How did you end up working in this field?

Korean: 그 논의는 결과적으로 기대보다 더 유익했어요.
English: The discussion ended up being more useful than I expected.
The meeting turned out to be shorter than expected.

Korean: 알고 보니 아침 식사가 포함되어 있네요.
English: It turns out that breakfast is included.
I'm glad everything turned out well.
The repair turned out to cost less than we thought.

Korean: 주요 차이점을 짚어 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you point out the main differences?
She pointed out a mistake in the report.

Korean: 아직 시간이 있다는 점을 말씀드리고 싶어요.
English: I'd like to point out that we still have time.

Korean: 그는 지도에서 가장 좋은 경로를 짚어 줬어요.
English: He pointed out the best route on the map.
I need to cut down on coffee in the afternoon.
We're trying to cut down on unnecessary spending.

Korean: 기차를 타면 이동 비용을 줄일 수 있어요.
English: Taking the train helps cut down on travel costs.
I'd like to cut down on the time I spend on my phone.
Would you mind taking off your shoes?

Korean: 우리 비행기는 삼십 분 늦게 이륙했어요.
English: Our flight took off thirty minutes late.

Korean: 인터뷰 이후 그녀의 사업이 크게 성장했어요.
English: Her business really took off after the interview.
I'm taking Friday off to spend time with my family.

Korean: 제가 없는 동안 그가 프로젝트를 맡겠다고 했어요.
English: He offered to take over the project while I was away.

Korean: 몇 분 동안 대신 맡아 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you take over for a few minutes?

Korean: 더 큰 회사가 그 사업체를 인수했어요.
English: A larger company took over the business.
She'll take over as team leader next month.
I'm thinking of taking up swimming.

Korean: 이 소파는 공간을 너무 많이 차지해요.
English: This sofa takes up too much space.

Korean: 도와주셔서 감사해요. 시간을 많이 뺏지는 않을게요.
English: Thanks for your help; I won't take up much of your time.

Korean: 그녀는 은퇴 후 사진 촬영을 시작했어요.
English: She took up photography after retiring.
I find it hard to put up with constant interruptions.
We had to put up with the noise during the renovation.
You shouldn't have to put up with rude behavior.

Korean: 알려만 주시면 잠깐 늦는 건 괜찮아요.
English: I can put up with a short delay if you let me know.
I'll call you back as soon as I'm free.

Korean: 그녀에게 다시 전화해 달라고 전해 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you ask her to call me back?

Korean: 고객센터에서 한 시간 안에 다시 전화하겠다고 했어요.
English: Customer service said they would call back within an hour.

Korean: 어제 그에게 다시 전화하는 걸 잊었어요.
English: I forgot to call him back yesterday.
We had to call off the picnic because of the rain.
They called off the meeting at the last minute.
Let's not call it off until we've checked the weather.
The event was called off due to safety concerns.
Don't hang up; I'll check that for you.

Korean: 그녀가 말을 마치기 전에 실수로 전화를 끊었어요.
English: I accidentally hung up before she finished speaking.
He hung up as soon as the call was over.

Korean: 전화를 끊고 대신 이 번호로 전화해 주세요.
English: Please hang up and call this number instead.
Could you hold on for a moment?
Hold on to the receipt in case you need a refund.

Korean: 잠깐만요. 한 단계를 빠뜨린 것 같아요.
English: Hold on; I think we've missed a step.
You should hold on to the handrail on the stairs.
My car broke down on the way to work.

Korean: 총비용을 항목별로 설명해 주실 수 있나요?
English: Could you break down the total cost for me?
The discussion broke down over the payment terms.

Korean: 이 일을 더 작은 단계로 나눠 봐요.
English: Let's break down this task into smaller steps.

Korean: 오늘 아침에 흥미로운 기사를 우연히 발견했어요.
English: I came across an interesting article this morning.

Korean: 그녀는 청소하다가 옛 사진 몇 장을 발견했어요.
English: She came across some old photos while cleaning.

Korean: 더 저렴한 선택지를 발견하면 알려 주세요.
English: Let me know if you come across a cheaper option.

Korean: 그는 친절하고 편하게 대화할 수 있는 사람처럼 보였어요.
English: He came across as friendly and easy to talk to.
I need to go over the notes before the presentation.

Korean: 세부 사항을 한 번 더 확인해 봐요.
English: Let's go over the details one more time.

Korean: 그녀가 저와 함께 안내 사항을 확인했어요.
English: She went over the instructions with me.

Korean: 합의한 내용을 다시 확인할 수 있을까요?
English: Could we go over what we've agreed on?

Korean: 직장에서 스트레스가 많은 시기를 보내고 있어요.
English: I've been going through a stressful period at work.

Korean: 서명하기 전에 문서를 꼼꼼히 확인해 주세요.
English: Please go through the document before signing.
The payment finally went through.

Korean: 우리는 매달 프린터 용지를 많이 써요.
English: We go through a lot of printer paper each month.

Korean: 예약 시간보다 십 분 일찍 와 주세요.
English: Please show up ten minutes before your appointment.

Korean: 그는 오지도 않았고 이유를 설명하는 전화도 하지 않았어요.
English: He didn't show up or call to explain.
Only a few people showed up for the workshop.
The error doesn't show up until I restart the app.
I'll try to make up for the time we lost.

Korean: 그녀는 늦은 이유를 설명하려고 이야기를 지어냈어요.
English: She made up a story to explain why she was late.
We argued yesterday, but we've made up now.

Korean: 작은 지출들이 제 예산에서 큰 비중을 차지해요.
English: Small expenses make up a large part of my budget.

Korean: 그 강좌에 대해 더 알아보고 싶어요.
English: I'd like to find out more about the course.

Korean: 그 가게가 이전했다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
English: We found out that the store had moved.

Korean: 다음 열차가 언제 출발하는지 알아봐 주실 수 있나요?
English: Can you find out when the next train leaves?
I'll find out whether we need to bring anything.
